speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have been experiencing difficulties conceiving and discomfort during sexual activity; to help identify the underlying cause, please describe the specific nature and location of your pain during intercourse. Additionally, have you noticed any abnormal discharge, bleeding, or changes in your menstrual cycle?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the pelvic floor tension and difficulty conceiving, have you ever experienced dyspareunia (pain with intercourse) before, and have you noticed any deep pain specifically during ovulation or at the end of your period? Additionally, has a pelvic ultrasound or pap smear been performed recently to rule out structural causes?

speaker: Patient
text: he is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Dyspareunia secondary to pelvic floor dysfunction.
